title: Quickstart visual playbook for structured output (schema examples + validation UI)
creator: Lena Cho
description: Design a concise visual playbook and in-product screenshots for the quickstart section that teaches users how to author structured output JSON schemas, see live validation, and reuse example templates. Deliver a set of annotated screenshots, Figma components, copy variants, and accessibility checks to hand off to docs and engineering.
acceptance_criteria: Three annotated hero screenshots (1200x630) showing: schema editor, live validation panel, example responses
Figma file with reusable components: schema token, validation badge, example gallery card, copy variants; components must be auto-layout enabled
Copy variants A/B ready for quick AB test in docs (short, medium, verbose)
A working design spec for engineering: component states, responsive breakpoints, keyboard nav and ARIA notes
All images exported in webp and png and uploaded to Drive with clear naming and layer references
Design accepted by PM and runtime engineering with at most 2 rounds of changes
tasks: Create initial sketches of schema editor and validation UI
Build Figma components and example gallery cards
Produce annotated hero screenshots for docs and landing pages
Compile handoff package (assets, tokens, export notes) and upload to Drive
Run accessibility review with A11y checklist and record fixes
Gather engineering feasibility feedback and update spacing/typography tokens
screenshots: hero_schema_editor_v1.png - shows inline schema suggestions and example dropdown
validation_panel_live_error.png - demonstrates schema validation error mapping to response fields
example_gallery_response_card.png - showcases templated schemas for invoices, tickets, and product specs
comments: 2025-02-11 Lena Cho: Initial sketches uploaded to Figma; focused on showing both schema and example output side-by-side.
2025-02-13 Marco Ruiz (Eng): Confirmed that the inline validation error mapping is feasible but needs a compact error format for high token workloads. Engineering requests JSONPath for error anchors.
2025-02-15 Priya Rao (PM): Suggests adding a small microcopy line 'Start from an example' to reduce cognitive load for new users. Also asked for A/B copy variants.
2025-02-18 Asha Patel: Updated Figma with accessible color tokens and added keyboard nav states to the schema editor component.
2025-02-21 Design-review: Left two UI notes — reduce left gutter by 8px, make validation badges 2px taller to match token set. Ready for final export once PRD links are attached.
decisions: Use a collapsible right-side 'Examples' panel in quickstart to avoid overwhelming first-time users
Validation errors will surface inline with a compact summary and a hover/expand to show full JSONPath and example mismatch
Export screenshots at 1200x630 for marketing/docs and 1024x576 for in-product help overlays
Keep schema editor as a monospaced token area with syntax highlighting and an 'Apply Example' one-click action
handoff_links: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1284 - PR with doc quickstart copy and screenshots
https://github.com/redwood-inference/webapp/pull/2890 - front-end component spec for schema editor
notes: Engineering asked for JSONPath anchors in error payloads; follow-up ticket ENG-4292 suggested for runtime changes. We intentionally keep examples small (≤ 6 keys) for first-run onboarding. Consider adding a 'try it with your data' CTA in next iteration.
review_feedback: PM (Priya Rao): Tighten copy on the hero screenshot — replace 'Try Structured Output' with 'Validate JSON schema' for clarity
Eng (Marco Ruiz): Add a compact error token format 'field: error' to reduce payloads; deferred full JSONPath expansion to hover interactions
Security (Amir Khan): No PII in example responses; all sample data sanitized. Confirmed.
